author: BBC News
description:
Former top US health official Anthony Fauci has refused to answer questions at a tense US Senate hearing on Covid-19, saying he feared Republicans would try to use his testimony to prosecute him for perjury.
 
He invoked the Fifth Amendment to the US Constitution - which says nobody can be "compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself" - more than 100 times.
 
Republicans have long accused Fauci of concealing information about the pandemic from the public and lying about its dangers. He has denied wrongdoing.
 
Fauci has called the allegations against him "simply preposterous" in previous testimony to lawmakers.
 
Before leaving office in 2025, then-President Joe Biden issued a pre-emptive pardon to Fauci, granting him protection from any prosecution.

A teenager who travelled from Norway to the UK to carry out an assassination for a Swedish organised crime group has been found guilty of conspiracy to murder.

An Old Bailey jury heard how Johannes Natland, 19, was arrested in a hotel room in Huddersfield with two working guns and 19 rounds of live ammunition in March 2025.

He pleaded guilty to possession of the firearms and ammunition but had denied the conspiracy charge.

Following a retrial, Natland showed no emotion as the jury brought in a unanimous guilty verdict after deliberating for just over 17 hours.

During the trial opening, prosecutor Alistair Richardson said the teen was "recruited" by the Foxtrot Network, which was described as a Swedish organised crime group backed by the Iranian regime.

Natland had claimed rather than carry out the attack, he had planned to shoot himself in the foot, telling jurors he had found himself in "a major pickle".

description:
US President Donald Trump has vowed to hit Iran hard after a ballistic missile attack on US bases overnight in Jordan. It's the first such attack since Trump ordered a halt to US strikes over the weekend. 
 
In response, the American and Saudi Arabian forces quickly launched joint strikes on militant groups in Iraq who are aligned with Iran. 
 
Twenty people were reportedly killed, including five Iranians. And the US President has threatened further strikes. 
 
Iraq - which is a key US ally in the region -  is furious, warning Washington and Riyadh it will defend its sovereignty against any further strikes. 

On the Iran War Today, we bring you up to date with everything you need to know about the conflict and what might come next.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants a major reform of the current social care system in England and set out his three-point plan to achieve it.

The prime minister has brought forward a review of social care by Baroness Casey, and has asked the Conservatives and the Liberal Democrats to work with him on his reforms.

But what does Andy Burnham mean by a ‘National Care Service’? Why have 22 previous reviews into adult social care failed to affect change? And how will he fund the major task of fixing social care in England?

description:
The BBC's chief football news reporter Simon Stone tells us about Fifa's controversial plan to sell stock in the World Cup. 

Football's global governing body is registered as a non-profit. But Fifa boss Gianni Infantino has proposed a new subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would sell shares to private investors, and run major events including the World Cup. 

Fifa says the lead investor would likely be Thrive Eternal, a US venture capital firm founded by Joshua Kushner - whose brother Jared Kushner is President Donald Trump's son-in-law. 

Mr Infantino has said that the individual football federations which make up Fifa stand to make an initial $20 million if they accept the plan. But Europe's UEFA - which is among the most powerful of those federations - has said the proposal "crosses a line", accusing Fifa of using football "to enrich themselves and their friends".

description:
Saudi Arabia and the US have carried out strikes against Iran-backed militias in Iraq, in a potential escalation of the Middle East conflict.

US Central Command said the strikes were against "Iran-aligned terrorists that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps directed to attack US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure".

Iraq's paramilitary Popular Mobilisation Forces, which is dominated by Iran-backed Shia militias, said at least 20 of its members had been killed in US-Saudi strikes on its bases.

It came hours after Centcom said Iran had launched missiles at US forces in the Middle East in an "attempted surprise attack", ending a lull in hostilities.

Spanish authorities have allowed thousands of people evacuated because of wildfires to return to their homes after restrictions were lifted in the areas of Toledo, Madrid, Ávila, and Castellón.
 
In the Madrid region alone, 24,000 people have been told they can return and lockdowns on another 20,000 have been lifted.
 
Spain and France are both braced for the start of the fourth heatwave so far this summer and some fires have continued to burn, including one at Burgohondo 150km (93 miles) west of Madrid.

description:
Warning: This video contains details of alleged sexual offences and misconduct.
 
Hollywood actor and musician Jared Leto is facing allegations of criminal sexual conduct by four women who were all teenagers at the time of the alleged offences.
 
The actor, who won an Oscar in 2014 for his role in ‘Dallas Buyers Club' made his name with films like Requiem for a Dream, the Suicide Squad and more recently Tron: Ares.
 
His rock band '30 Seconds to Mars' are planning a high-profile tour next spring. The women who spoke to the BBC said they encountered the 54-year-old between 2002 and 2014. 
 
Despite repeated attempts to contact Jared Leto, he has not responded to the allegations put to him by the BBC.

Thirteen people have died in an earthquake that struck south-west Japan, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi says, adding that rescuers are in a "race against time".
 
Rescue efforts are underway at a shopping mall in Kumamoto, where many people are trapped.
 
Earlier, a Japanese official told the BBC that multiple people are unaccounted for at the centre, and at a factory after a chimney collapsed.
 
The earthquake - estimated at 6.8 magnitude by the US Geological Survey - hit inland on Kyushu island at 16:27 local time (07:27 GMT) on Tuesday.
